title: PowerToys Monaco Preview Handler displays UTF-16LE .reg files with NUL characters
author: Jordi-PAPA

status.label: Actionable encoding defect
status.detail: The reporter supplied a sample, workaround, and latest-version confirmation; source shows a decoded-text-to-original-encoding transport seam that needs design validation.

next_action.label: Complete encoding design
next_action.reason: Specify the Monaco payload encoding contract and regression tests before approval.

judgment.rationale: The report is reproducible on the latest stable version and source inspection identifies a focused encoding boundary suitable for implementation-grade design.
evidence: The attached UTF-16LE .reg sample displays visible NUL markers in Monaco but displays correctly through the built-in Windows text preview handler.
The reporter manually updated to 0.101.2362.0 and confirmed the issue still reproduces.

MonacoPreviewHandlerControl decodes through CharsetDetector and StreamReader, then base64-encodes encodingToUse.GetBytes(fileContent); src/Monaco/index.html decodes PT_CODE as UTF-8-like percent-encoded bytes.
judgment.recommended_action: Develop an implementation-grade design that normalizes the decoded text for Monaco transport and adds UTF-16LE/UTF-16BE/UTF-8 regression coverage.

issue_context.summary: Monaco correctly receives a UTF-16LE Registry file but renders each zero byte as a visible NUL marker instead of normal decoded text.
known_information: The issue includes a minimal UTF-16LE .reg reproduction archive and a workaround archive removing HKCU Monaco preview-handler overrides.
UTF-8 content renders correctly, and disabling Monaco lets the built-in Windows preview handler render the UTF-16LE file correctly.
The reporter confirmed the defect on PowerToys 0.101.2362.0 after manually updating.
There are no assignees, linked fixes, or comments after the latest-version confirmation.
inferences: The WebView payload likely expects UTF-8 byte semantics or decoded character text while receiving UTF-16LE bytes, which would explain alternating visible NUL markers.
Encoding detection may be succeeding; the defect may occur after decoding when the text is re-encoded for PT_CODE.
issue_context.analysis: The reporter closed the version and reproduction gaps. The source path gives a concrete hypothesis, so fast triage should route design work rather than ask for another diagnostic archive.
initial_investigation: Forced 2026-09-02 pass read the complete issue body, both comments, labels, empty assignee list, and timeline links; no linked work appeared.

Read src/modules/previewpane/MonacoPreviewHandler/MonacoPreviewHandlerControl.cs around CharsetDetector.DetectFromFile, StreamReader decoding, and Convert.ToBase64String(encodingToUse.GetBytes(fileContent)).
Read src/Monaco/index.html, where [[PT_CODE]] is decoded with atob plus decodeURIComponent over percent-encoded bytes.

Forced second pass on 2026-09-02 re-read the complete report, both comments, labels, empty assignee list, and timeline and checked Monaco handler history, including the prior UTF-8 BOM fix #39381; no linked fix addresses UTF-16 payload transport.

information_gaps.why_needed: It determines whether the handler should always encode UTF-8 bytes, escape decoded Unicode text differently, or adjust the page decoder.
information_gaps.information: The exact JavaScript decoding contract for the PT_CODE payload after decoded .NET text is injected.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Trace the Monaco index template payload decode and add round-trip tests for UTF-8, UTF-16LE with BOM, and UTF-16BE.
